newsitem.title: USA: Clinton asks for disaster bill without riders.
newsitem.headline: Clinton asks for disaster bill without riders.

text.p: President Clinton urged the Republican-led Congress on Tuesday to give him a straightforward disaster relief bill, uncluttered with political riders, to help natural disasster victims in 35 states.

Clinton made his appeal a day after he vetoed an $8.6 billion emergency money bill, saying it was loaded with congressional Republicans' pet projects. "Just send me a straighforward disaster relief bill," he said.

The bill provided $5.4 billion for disaster assistance, including $89 million for House Speaker Newt Gingrich's home state of Georgia and $24 million for Senate Republican Leader Trent Lott's state of Mississippi.

Clinton, who visited flood-ravaged North Dakota April 22, huffed to a Rose Garden ceremony on education standards: "It has been 80 days since I forwarded to Congress my request for disaster relief to allow the process of recovery to begin.

"Instead of giving me a disaster relief bill, the congressional majority insisted on weighing it down on a political wish list. In the name of the people who had to face the floods, in the name of the people who need their help now, I ask the majority to put aside the political game, to set aside the political wish list."
Of all the attached riders, Clinton said, "We can negotiate on all this later."
